result.notes:
I booked part one of the old organizations concept. There are 147 records:
- data.ts: 19 tables and 14 machines. These cover every table in packages/backend/src/organizations/tables/ and every literal-union status field in the whole concept.
- procedures.ts: 60 procedures, covering every door function that is not a pure rule. This includes all 11 stand-ins in payments/neighbors.ts, with the same ids and export names.
- setups.ts: 17 rpcs and 2 workflows.
- workspaces.ts: 2 rpcs. treasuries.ts: 2 rpcs. roles.ts: 1 rpc.
- members.ts: 8 rpcs and 1 workflow.
- invitations.ts: 16 rpcs and 1 workflow.
- flows.ts: 4 flows.
- reads.ts: no new records (it re-exports procedures).
- index.ts: lists my files and part two's.

Checks:
- `tsc -p books` shows only unresolved imports from lanes that have not written those files yet (listed under missing).
- I mirrored the book in the scratchpad with stubs for those names. All 10 of my modules load there and every record passes its schema check at load time.
- A build of my lane alone found no machine-state problems. Its "unreachable-state" gaps are real findings: org-member's pending and pending_safe states, org-role's revoked state, and org-roles-deployment's requested and failed states are never written.
- Every transition still marked undriven belongs to part two's machines (director changes, share transfers, votes). Part two's files already import my table and machine names, and all of them match.

Judgments I made:
1. The reads area (src/organizations/reads/) has no operations; its functions are door functions. reads.ts only re-exports those procedures from procedures.ts and adds no records.
2. Machine id is the singular of the table name in kebab case: org-lifecycle, org-member, seat-permission-change, org-invitation and so on. A second status field on the same table gets `<entity>-<field>`: org-invitation-delivery and org-invitation-cleanup. Transition names keep the old state literals, so the setup machine has `to_awaitingAuthorization` and `to_needsAttention`.
3. No old writer inserts a member row as pending, pending_safe or pending_grant; those are legacy states. org-member therefore starts at active, and the moves out of the legacy states (advance, sweep, grant application) are still booked.
4. Four door functions run from an action rather than in a transaction: `requireSafeOwner`, `settleOrganizationProposals` and `readTreasuryTarget`. `deliverInvitationOutcome` runs in a transaction but queues an email through the Resend component. All four are booked as procedures, and their `about` says so. The first two carry the touches of part two's proposals load and settle.
5. A few integration calls may not be booked yet, so I reference them through a small `callOf`/`fnOf` helper. It returns the shared record's call when it exists and otherwise a ref with the id that record will carry, so the build flags it if it never appears. I left out `companyMintCall` because it only builds calldata and reaches nothing outside.
6. `setups.get` and `invitations.get` are booked as kind `live`, because the SDK subscribes to both.
7. `observe` (scheduled by every check write) and `recover` (cron every minute) are workflows. So are `invitations.expire` (daily at 00:00 UTC) and `members.notify-permission` (scheduled when a grant is applied). observe's trigger is accept-authorization; its other schedulers are named in `about`.
   - observe has `retries.max` 2 because recovery reschedules a lapsed check twice and halts it on the third.
   - The 600000 ms timeouts are Convex's action limit, the same value payments used; the old code sets none.
8. All emit-* operations are rpcs whose `about` starts with "Telemetry plumbing:".
9. Work the old code schedules into Permissions (`permissions.grants.drive` and `permissions.grants.retry`) is named in prose only, not linked.
10. I set no budgets. Backend rpc spans are empty because no child spans were known; I named the SDK operation spans where the code opens one.

Findings to note:
- Payments, Permissions' guards, Requests, Indexing drifts and Books' keepers read orgs, orgMembers and orgLifecycles directly instead of through the door. I recorded this in the table descriptions; the write-boundary report belongs to those lanes.
- index.ts imports part two's flows-governance.ts, which does not exist yet.
